source.credit: Morgado et al. (2021), Astronomy & Astrophysics 652, A141; Santos-Sanz et al. (2025), arXiv:2510.06366v1 for the 2022 JWST ring measurements.

constraints.axisConvention: Full axes are halved exactly. +Z is the adopted pole; +X is the arbitrary display meridian.
constraints.qualification: Triaxial ellipsoid fitted jointly to eleven stellar occultations in 2013–2020, with semiaxes 143.8, 135.2 and 99.1 km (Morgado et al. 2021, Table 6). The smooth approximation does not resolve topography. The axes are model estimates, rather than three independently measured diameters.
constraints.scale: The reference radius is the geometric mean of the approximation semiaxes. It is a rendering scale, not an independent measured mean radius or convex-model volume.

assumptions: Triaxial ellipsoid fitted jointly to eleven stellar occultations in 2013–2020, with semiaxes 143.8, 135.2 and 99.1 km (Morgado et al. 2021, Table 6). The smooth approximation does not resolve topography. The axes are model estimates, rather than three independently measured diameters.

The ICRS ring-plane normal is RA 151.03° ± 0.14°, Dec +41.81° ± 0.07°. The body spin axis is assumed to share that normal, as in the published shape fit. The direction of angular momentum is unknown; the positive-declination pole is the paper's arbitrary choice. The photometric period is an approximate spin rate, not a precise sidereal rotational ephemeris. The displayed longitude origin and rotational phase are arbitrary.
approximation.qualification: Observation-constrained ellipsoid; no invented local terrain or albedo.

spin.meaning: The ICRS ring-plane normal is RA 151.03° ± 0.14°, Dec +41.81° ± 0.07°. The body spin axis is assumed to share that normal, as in the published shape fit. The direction of angular momentum is unknown; the positive-declination pole is the paper's arbitrary choice. The photometric period is an approximate spin rate, not a precise sidereal rotational ephemeris. The displayed longitude origin and rotational phase are arbitrary.

unresolved: Local surface topography is not recoverable from the selected global ellipsoid fit.

The rings vary with longitude, wavelength and epoch. Two concentric circular annuli approximate the 2022 JWST first-contact dimensions; widths and fixed display opacities are not a view-dependent scattering model.
The body spin direction and absolute rotational phase are not measured by these inputs.
